title: Module 3: Create Application and Modules
description: Creating scoped applications in ServiceNow Studio, application scope and namespaces, the extend-vs-create data model decision, default fields and inheritance, application access and cross-scope privileges, application menus and modules, and deployment via update sets and the application repository.

questions.prompt: How is the scope (namespace) prefix of a new scoped application constructed?

choices.text: x_ + the glide.appcreator.company.code value + a truncated application name
The full application name, lowercased, with spaces replaced by underscores
global_ followed by the developer's user ID and then the full application name
A random GUID assigned at creation time

questions.explanation: Scope is built automatically as x_ + the glide.appcreator.company.code value + a truncated application name (e.g. x_cdltd_loaner_r_0). If a truncated name collides with an existing app, the appended number increments.

questions.prompt: Which statement about the glide.appcreator.company.code system property is correct?

choices.text: It is set by ServiceNow and is not user-changeable, and is typically 2 to 5 characters long
Developers are expected to change it for each new application to avoid scope collisions entirely
It is always exactly the same as the application's sys_id
It only applies to applications built in the global scope

questions.explanation: The company code property is set by ServiceNow, is not user-changeable, and is typically 2 to 5 characters. It becomes part of every scoped app's namespace and must match across instances for the application repository to work.

questions.prompt: When you create a new scoped application in ServiceNow Studio, which roles does it create by default?

choices.text: An Admin role and a User role
Only the system administrator (admin) role
No roles; you must always create them manually
An Approver role and a Fulfiller role

questions.explanation: Studio creates a scoped Admin role and a User role by default. You can keep them, delete them, or assign existing roles instead. The created Admin role is an application admin role, not the platform-wide sysadmin role.

questions.prompt: A developer extends an existing table to create a new child table. What does the child table contain immediately after creation?

choices.text: The parent's columns but none of the parent's data (no rows)
A full copy of the parent's columns and all of its existing records
Only the six default audit fields and nothing inherited
A live reference to the parent's rows that updates automatically

questions.explanation: Extending copies the parent's structure (columns), not its data. The child table starts empty. It also inherits the parent's server-side business logic, such as business rules and ACLs.

questions.prompt: When a table extends a parent table, which behaviors are inherited automatically (for free) versus optionally? Select all statements that are TRUE. (Choose 2)

choices.text: Server-side business logic such as business rules and access controls is inherited automatically
Client-side logic such as UI policies and client scripts can be inherited, controlled by a field on each such record
The parent's records (rows of data) are inherited along with the columns
Inheritance of business rules must be enabled individually on each child table

questions.explanation: Extending inherits the parent's server-side customizations (business rules, ACLs) automatically. Client-side records like UI policies and client scripts have a field that determines whether they apply to extended tables, so that inheritance is optional. Data (rows) is never inherited.

questions.prompt: Which condition must be met before a table can be extended by another table?

choices.text: The table must have the Extensible option selected
The table must contain at least one record
The table must be in the global scope
The table must already have auto-numbering configured

questions.explanation: A table must have Extensible selected to be extended. You also cannot extend a system table or a database view table.

questions.prompt: Which type of table CANNOT be extended?

choices.text: A database view table
A table that extends the Task table
A custom table created from scratch with Extensible selected
A table that already has child tables

questions.explanation: System tables and database view tables cannot be extended. A custom or extended table can itself be extended as long as it is marked Extensible.

questions.prompt: Most approval workflow activities work only on which tables?

choices.text: Tables that extend the Task table
Any table in any scope
Only the global cmdb_ci table
Only tables created from scratch (not extended)

questions.explanation: All approval activities except the User Approval activity work only on tables that extend Task. The User Approval activity works with all tables. This is a key reason to extend Task when modeling assignable work.

questions.prompt: Which fields are created by default on EVERY new table? (Choose 3)

choices.text: Sys ID (sys_id)
Updates (sys_mod_count)
Created by (sys_created_by)
Class (sys_class_name)

questions.explanation: Every table gets six default audit fields: sys_id, sys_created_by, sys_created_on, sys_updated_by, sys_updated_on, and sys_mod_count. The Class (sys_class_name) field is only added when the table is marked Extensible.

questions.prompt: Under what condition is the Class field (sys_class_name) added to a table?

choices.text: When the table is marked Extensible
On every table by default
Only when the table has auto-numbering enabled
Only on database view tables

questions.explanation: If a table is extensible, a Class (sys_class_name) field is added to indicate which child table actually contains each record. It is not one of the six standard default fields.

questions.prompt: What data type is the sys_id field?

choices.text: A GUID (unique record identifier)
A glide_date_time timestamp
A numeric counter
A reference to the sys_user table

questions.explanation: sys_id is a GUID that uniquely identifies every record in every table, automatically populated by the system on insert.

questions.prompt: Application Access settings on a table primarily provide what kind of protection?

choices.text: Runtime protection governing access from scripts in other scopes and from web service calls
Design-time protection preventing other developers from opening the table in Studio
Encryption of the table's data at rest
Row-level security based on the logged-in user's group membership

questions.explanation: Application Access provides runtime protection of application tables against read/write/create/delete operations coming from scripts and web service calls, and governs cross-scope and integration access. It is distinct from ACL/role-based record security.

questions.prompt: The 'Can read/create/update/delete' Application Access options control access for which callers?

choices.text: Scripts from OTHER application scopes; they never apply to the application's own scope
Access is limited only to users who currently hold the application's own admin role here
Absolutely all users on the instance, regardless of their scope or role assignments anywhere
Only scheduled jobs running in the global scope

questions.explanation: These options allow scripts from other application scopes to perform database operations on the table. They never apply to the current application's own scope, which always has access to its own tables.

questions.prompt: For a cross-scope privilege to let Application B access Application A's data, what must happen? (Choose 2)

choices.text: Application A's developer must allow application access so others can request permission
Application B's developer must request permission via a cross scope privilege record
Both applications must be merged into a single scope
Both applications must be published to the ServiceNow Store first

questions.explanation: Cross-scope access must be allowed on both sides: the owning app (A) enables Application Access so others can ask, and the requesting app (B) asks for permission through a cross scope privilege record. After publication, runtime requests run only if a valid cross-scope privilege record exists.

questions.prompt: When a table is created, what is the default name of the module created for it?

choices.text: The plural form of the table's name
The table's name with the scope prefix removed
Always 'All Records'
The singular form of the application menu's name

questions.explanation: The default module name is the plural of the table name (e.g. a Shipping table yields a Shippings module). It displays a list of all records from the table and can be renamed by editing the module.

questions.prompt: On a module record, what happens if the Roles field is left blank?

choices.text: The application's roles are inherited and the module is visible to all users who have them
The module becomes hidden from absolutely everyone, including every system administrator here
Only a full system administrator account is able to see this module in the navigator at all
The module is automatically deleted

questions.explanation: If Roles is blank, the module inherits the application's roles. Populating Roles restricts the module to those specific roles.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of the 'Override application menu roles' option on a module?

choices.text: It lets users open the module even without access to the containing menu, subject to the module's own roles.
It removes all role requirements from the module entirely
It hides the module from the application menu entirely, but keeps it accessible only through a direct URL.
It grants the module's roles to the parent application menu

questions.explanation: Override application menu roles allows a user to open the module even if they cannot see the containing menu. The user must still satisfy the module's own Roles requirement.

questions.prompt: On a module, which field is the key field that determines what kind of link the module opens (for example, a list of records or a new record form)?

choices.text: Link type
Order
Hint
Active

questions.explanation: Link type specifies what the module opens (List of Records, New Record, etc.). Depending on the link type, additional fields such as Filter, Content Page, or Arguments may be required.

questions.prompt: In the main ServiceNow window, what does a red ring around the scope selection (globe) icon indicate?

choices.text: You are NOT in the global scope (you are in a custom application scope)
An error has occurred with the current application or its configuration somewhere
The current update set has been completed and is now fully locked from editing
Domain separation is currently disabled on this instance for all users here

questions.explanation: A red ring around the globe means you are working in a custom (non-global) application scope, a visual reminder to confirm you are creating records in the intended scope.

questions.prompt: The scope selection menu in the main ServiceNow window provides which pickers? (Choose 3)

choices.text: Application scope
Update set
Domain scope
JavaScript mode

questions.explanation: The scope selection menu exposes the Application scope, Update set, and Domain scope pickers (domain only appears with domain separation). JavaScript mode is switched from the application's App settings, not this menu.

questions.prompt: Which capability does ServiceNow Studio NOT provide, requiring a different mechanism?

choices.text: Pushing application files to an external source control repository
Cross-scope development spanning both the global and custom application scopes here
Full code search running across all of the application's files at once
Deployment to other target instances through standard update set files

questions.explanation: Studio cannot push to external source control; update sets are used instead. It also does not provide script intellectual-property protection. It does support cross-scope development, code search, and deployment via update sets or the internal application repository.

questions.prompt: What is an update set?

choices.text: A container capturing customizations (config changes), exportable as XML
A scheduled backup of the instance's table data and all record contents only
A scheduled job that applies patches automatically
A role that grants deployment permissions

questions.explanation: An update set is a container for capturing customizations, stored on the sys_update_xml table and exportable as XML. By default it captures configuration changes, not data.

questions.prompt: By default, what does an update set capture?

choices.text: Customizations and configurations, but not data
Both the customizations and all of the table's data records
Only the actual data records themselves, never any configuration
Only the application's roles and nothing else at all here

questions.explanation: By default an update set captures customizations and configurations; data is not included unless specifically arranged.

questions.prompt: What does the 'Publish to Update Set' action on an application do?

choices.text: Packages the whole current app into a new Completed update set (a full snapshot, not a delta)
Captures only the application files that have changed since the last update set was marked completed
Permanently deletes the entire application from the instance right after it has been exported to XML
Publishes the application directly to the ServiceNow Store

questions.explanation: Publish to Update Set copies the latest version of every application file into a new update set and marks it Complete. It is a full snapshot, not a delta, which makes it useful as an initial 'commit' right after creating an app.

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the relationship between application scope and update sets?

choices.text: Update sets are subservient to scope; one scope can contain several update sets
Each individual update set can span across multiple application scopes simultaneously at once
An application scope can belong to only one update set at a time
Scope and update set are two names for the same container

questions.explanation: Scope is the larger, umbrella container; update sets live within a scope, and a scope can contain several. Because creating an app starts a new scope, an update set started beforehand would not capture the app itself.

questions.prompt: Setting an update set's State to 'Complete' has what effect?

choices.text: It closes the update set and makes it retrievable on a connected instance
It immediately deploys the changes to every instance in the stack
It permanently deletes the update set after export
It reverts all changes captured in the update set

questions.explanation: Marking an update set Complete stops the 'recording' of changes and makes it retrievable from a connected instance so it can be previewed and committed there.

questions.prompt: What is the correct order of the final steps when deploying an update set onto a target instance?

choices.text: Retrieve, then preview, then commit
Commit, then preview, then retrieve
Preview, then commit, then retrieve
Retrieve, then commit, then preview

questions.explanation: On the target, you retrieve the completed update set, preview it to catch problems (such as references to tables that do not exist on the target), and then commit it.

questions.prompt: The system property glide.update_set.auto_preview is set to true. What happens after an update set is retrieved on the target instance?

choices.text: The preview process starts automatically
The update set is committed automatically without preview
The update set is rejected and must be re-retrieved
The update set is exported back to the source instance

questions.explanation: If glide.update_set.auto_preview is true, the preview starts automatically after retrieval. If false, you must start the preview manually. Preview never auto-commits.

questions.prompt: What is the guidance on moving update sets between instances running different family releases?

choices.text: Older-to-newer loads are always fine, but newer-to-older loads need extra testing and risk outages or data loss.
Update sets can only ever be moved between instances running the exact same family release version, never otherwise.
Newer-to-older transfers are always perfectly safe, while older-to-newer transfers are blocked entirely by the platform
Family release has no bearing on update set compatibility

questions.explanation: You can always load an update set from an older family release onto a newer-release instance. Loading a newer-release set onto an older-release instance requires additional testing and, in extreme cases, can cause outages or data loss, so moving updates from newer to older releases should be avoided.

questions.prompt: What is the application repository used for?

choices.text: A central store distributing an org's published scoped apps between its own instances (dev, test, prod)
A public marketplace for selling apps to any company
An external Git-based service used for source-controlling all of an application's files and metadata over time
A backup location for table data only

questions.explanation: The application repository is a central store for an organization's published scoped applications, used to promote apps between that organization's own instances. You can only see and manage apps published by your own organization.

questions.prompt: Which conditions are required for an instance to use the application repository? (Choose 3)

choices.text: A valid subscription
A matching glide.appcreator.company.code value across instances
Network access
A connection to an external source control system

questions.explanation: Using the application repository requires a valid subscription, network access, and a matching application scope/company code across instances. As a result, personal developer instances cannot connect to it. Source control is unrelated.

questions.prompt: Why can a personal developer instance (PDI) not connect to the application repository?

choices.text: It lacks the valid subscription, matching scope, and network access the repository requires
A standalone PDI simply does not support scoped applications in the first place at all anywhere
Personal developer instances are completely unable to create update sets of any kind at all
The repository only accepts global-scope applications

questions.explanation: The application repository requires a valid subscription, matching application scope, and network access. A standalone PDI does not meet these requirements, so it cannot connect.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between rolling back and uninstalling an application deployed via the application repository?

choices.text: Roll back reverts to the previous version; uninstall removes the app from the instance but leaves it in the repository.
Roll back permanently deletes the app from the central repository, whereas uninstall only hides it from view temporarily
They are identical operations with different names
Roll back removes the app permanently; uninstall cannot be undone

questions.explanation: Roll back returns the app to its previous installation and does not affect the global application record. Uninstall removes the app from the instance but not from the repository, so it can be reinstalled later.

questions.prompt: Which sharing method would you use to make an application available for purchase by other companies?

choices.text: Publish to the ServiceNow Store
Publish to an update set
Publish to the application repository
Export the table data as CSV

questions.explanation: The ServiceNow Store is the public marketplace for sharing or selling apps to other companies. Update sets and the application repository keep distribution within your own organization/stack.

questions.prompt: Which statement about publishing to the ServiceNow Store is correct?

choices.text: Apps are reviewed and certified by ServiceNow before becoming available, not published directly
Submitted apps appear in the ServiceNow Store instantly with no review or certification at all
Only applications that are completely free of charge may ever be published to the ServiceNow Store
ServiceNow assumes all testing responsibility on the buyer's behalf

questions.explanation: Store submissions are sent for review and certified by ServiceNow for best-practice compliance before listing; they are not published directly. Apps may be free or fee-based, and the buyer is responsible for testing and assumes the risk.

questions.prompt: What is the default JavaScript mode for a new scoped application?

choices.text: ECMAScript 2021 (ES12)
ECMAScript 5 (ES5)
ECMAScript 3 (ES3)
TypeScript

questions.explanation: The default JavaScript mode is ECMAScript 2021 (ES12). It can be switched from the application's App settings.

questions.prompt: Application files visible in an app's 'Application files' related list are records on which table?

choices.text: sys_metadata
sys_app
sys_update_xml
sys_user

questions.explanation: Application files are records on the sys_metadata table, shown filtered to the app's scope. The app record itself lives on sys_app, and update set contents live on sys_update_xml.

questions.prompt: How does App Engine Studio (AES) differ from ServiceNow Studio?

choices.text: AES is a guided low-code tool needing an App Engine subscription; Studio is a centralized pro-code IDE
App Engine Studio is the only available tool that is able to create new scoped applications on the platform
Studio is low-code and AES is pro-code
App Engine Studio is only ever able to run on personal developer instances and on nowhere else at all really

questions.explanation: App Engine Studio is a guided, low-code development tool that requires an App Engine subscription (or a product packaged with one). ServiceNow Studio is the centralized integrated tool for pro-code/traditional application development.

questions.prompt: You created a table and want other tables, including some in different application scopes, to be able to extend it. Which table setting makes this possible?

choices.text: Extensible
Extends table
Scriptable Table
Application Access

questions.explanation: Marking a table as extensible is what allows other tables, including those in different scopes, to inherit from it as a parent. The extends-table setting works in the opposite direction: it is where a child table selects the parent it inherits from. A scriptable table cannot be extended at all, so that setting is mutually exclusive with extension. The application-access settings govern cross-scope create, read, update, and delete operations, not whether a table can serve as a parent.

questions.prompt: When you create a new table and leave the option that also creates a module enabled, what does that generated module display by default?

choices.text: A list of all records in the table.
An empty form ready to create a new record.
An empty application homepage.
A help page describing how to configure the module.

questions.explanation: The auto-generated module opens a list view showing all records in the table, not a new-record form. The wording can mislead, because creating a module is about adding a navigation entry, not about creating a record. Pointing the module at a new-record form, a homepage, or a help page would all require additional configuration.

questions.prompt: Which applications appear in the Application Picker that a developer uses to set their current scope context?

choices.text: All custom application scopes plus the Global scope.
Every application on the instance, including baseline apps such as Incident.
Only custom applications the developer has created.
Only applications downloaded and installed from the Store.

questions.explanation: The Application Picker lists the custom application scopes plus Global, which is what a developer selects to set the scope their changes apply to. It is not a way to launch or browse every app on the instance, so baseline applications, a custom-only filter, or a downloaded-only filter do not describe it.
